title: Plain RLS at its best: tenant_id from the JWT claims and owner_id = auth.uid(), with composite btree indexes
issue: The control scenario. A tenant column compared with an InitPlan-wrapped JWT claim, and an owner column compared with (select auth.uid()), are the shapes Supabase recommends: the planner sees a plain equality on the leading column of a btree index and the policy costs nothing per row.
symptom: best_practice_rls should be within noise of no_rls_baseline on every query; naive_rls (unwrapped auth.jwt()) should be close for index scans but can lose estimates; best_practice_rls_membership (tenant looked up in a members table) adds a small InitPlan. pg_auth is expected to be close; the gap per query, including planning time, is the measurement.

scale.meaning: number of rows in app.events (and app.events_p). 30% belong to one large tenant; the rest are spread over scale/500 tenants (~350 rows each), 5 projects per tenant, 3 users per tenant, scale/2 notes. 10x = 2,000,000 events, 4,000 tenants, 1,000,000 notes; OpenFGA tuples grow only with tenants and users (3 members + 3 accounts per tenant: 24,000 at 10x).

subjects.name: large_tenant
subjects.note: user-0-0, member of tenant 0 (30% of all events)
